quick-summary.why: The single most important framing decision on this seat. The JD says '5+ years in deep learning / data engineering' - a compound OR whose halves must not be averaged. The summary now opens on data engineering as a through-line from 2012 to 2025 with three dated, concrete instances (master data management and field-level lineage at McDonald's 2012; entity resolution over 25 supplier catalogues on a 2-3 million-requests-a-day platform at Teletext 2016; PostgreSQL to Amazon Aurora at Deque through 2025), then arrives at the recent AI programme. Reading it top to bottom, the five-year bar is cleared on the data-engineering half before deep learning is mentioned. Python and FastAPI are named explicitly (journey doc line 678: '10-query decision-intelligence platform in Python (FastAPI, LangChain, LangGraph)').
quick-summary.heads_up: The deep-learning half is roughly 14 months, one programme - deliberately NOT stretched anywhere on this page. The IIIT PG Diploma (Jan 2021) sits in the education table and adds credibility, not years. Expect 'so how many years of deep learning is that, really?' and answer it as one intense year on top of a decade of the data engineering it sits on. Dropped from the summary: the Keycloak-to-Red-Hat-SSO line and the causal-inference sentence, because neither the SSO bullet nor the propensity-matching bullet is on this version.
quick-summary.hygiene: Expands AI and AWS on first use, and spells out 'retrieval-augmented generation' so the skills block can introduce the RAG abbreviation. Changed 'Cut infrastructure cost' to 'Brought infrastructure cost down' - Cut leads a Teletext bullet and that root echo was pre-existing in the master.

quick-vp.why: Ten bullets down to seven, and the first three are data engineering so the JD's compound requirement is answered before anything else. Every chat-platform bullet is gone (Kinesis shards, the Node.js-to-Go port, 100,000 concurrent connections, Datadog, patient onboarding) and the space went to the event spine, the nine-year hydration, tenant isolation at the columnar scan, the Python/FastAPI RAG pipeline, the SageMaker model ladder, the weekly retrain with drift triggers and batch-transform scoring, and Kubernetes/Terraform as a company-wide standard. Five bullets are drawn from master/merge_proposal.html Variant B; two are new (Hydrated, Triggered).
quick-vp.heads_up: Variant B was used deliberately, not A: the P99-under-200ms and NDCG 0.75 figures are pre-registered acceptance targets, not measurements, and this version does not carry them at all. Same discipline everywhere else here - there are NO Amura outcome metrics, only design and scale markers (nine years of history, 10 production pipelines, 30-day windows, P95 rebuild target, 80+ conditions). The three-model ladder describes the promotion GATE, not which rung is the live champion; kq4 says only 'the simplest model that cleared its bar', and 'so is a Transformer in production, or is it logistic regression?' is a near-certain question with no documented answer. Amura names no message broker at all - never cite it as Kinesis evidence; the Kinesis and high-availability work is the chat platform, a separate system. 'traversal-source wrapper' is written the way CLAUDE.md prescribes, since KQ9 words it 'tenant-scoped traversal-source wrapper' rather than by the TraversalSource class name. Kubernetes, Terraform, the 25-30% infrastructure cost and the under-10-minutes deploy time are user-confirmed 2026-08-25 and reach a résumé here for the first time; note that o9's JD names neither Kubernetes nor Terraform, so this bullet earns its place on MLOps and deployment infrastructure, not on keyword match.
quick-vp.hygiene: Seven bullets, all 25 words or fewer, each with a bolded fact and a numeric or scale marker, no trailing periods. New leading verbs Hydrated and Triggered were grepped stem-by-stem across all ten roles including the card-only pre-2016 ones and are clean. 'Sequenced' is gone with the old bullet, so it no longer collides with Sequence Mining.

quick-deque.why: Six bullets to seven, pulled from the eleven merged Deque bullets. This section is doing two jobs on this seat. First, it is the largest recent block on the résumé and a reader doing arithmetic on '5+ years of deep learning / data engineering' will land here - so it now leads with multi-tenant isolation at ~300 instances and the zero-downtime PostgreSQL-to-Aurora migration, which is data engineering with the only hard measured numbers in the block (backups 3-4 hours daily, deploy errors 40%). Second, Orchestrated is new to the résumé and is the strongest unstructured-data-pipeline evidence outside the AI programme: scheduled website-discovery and axe-core scanning, diffing consecutive runs. Exposed adds shared platform APIs across 20+ enterprise clients with versioning and backward compatibility - the platform-standards evidence the JD's leadership line asks for. Modernised adds the Jenkins-to-GitHub-Actions CI/CD work.
quick-deque.heads_up: The Jenkins-to-GitHub-Actions bullet is general CI/CD, NOT CI/CD for machine learning - Deque had no ML in it anywhere in the record. Do not let it be read as answering the JD's 'CI/CD for ML' line in a room. Two open confirm-or-reject items are on this block untouched and stay per the no-scrub rule: whether '~300' is customers or instances, and the 70-80% consolidation figure. Dropped for this seat: the Keycloak-to-Red-Hat-SSO bullet, the billing and subscription service, the Puppeteer regression framework, and the time-to-market bullet.
quick-deque.hygiene: Seven bullets, all 25 words or fewer. JWT and URLs expanded on first use; APIs and CI/CD use the short forms because the skills block now expands both. Orchestrated's scale marker is 'three states' (new, fixed, regressed) - the source records no run count or volume figure and none was invented.
